title: The empty place, the reshimu and the Kav: G-d hides Himself so that the work is ours
overview:
Chapter 13 is the *nimshal* of chapter 12's analogies. The *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui* is G-d hiding His essential light so that something that seems separate from Him can exist. But like the teacher who teaches in short, He loses nothing: the infinite light of the Essence is still there and unchanged, and "you can't not see G-d"; you just don't appreciate what you're seeing, like the cow on the eye doctor's card. That light is not even a *makif* on our world: it is like a person's taste, so the world expresses G-d but cannot define Him.

The *reshimu* is the power of the unlimited to limit itself, but it means that everything was removed, like a footprint. Truer likenesses are the craftsman's notes, the mnemonic, the thrown stone and the peace sign: the world looks like a system running on its own. Yet everything comes out of the *reshimu* through the *Kav*, as a house from its blueprint. G-d does not need a blueprint; He makes the world look fixed so that the *avoda* is ours. The purpose of man is to see past the first *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: The empty place: G-d hides His light, but it is still there, unchanged
sections.summary: The *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui* hides G-d's essential light so that something that seems separate from Him can exist and the light can later be revealed in it. But like the teacher who teaches in short, nothing is lost: the infinite light is still there, the darkness is only from our side, and what the *Kav* reveals is the very light that was before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.en: the *nimshal* for everything that we said in chapter 12 about the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu*,

phrases.he: יובן למעלה בכללות ענין הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי,
phrases.en: is understood in G-dliness about the *tzimtzum* that's called the *makom panui*; the *tzimtzum* is called the empty place.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת הסתלקות וההעלם לעצמותו כדי שיוכל להיות אחר כך בחינת השפעת אור כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: This idea of this *tzimtzum* is that G-d hides His essential light in order to be able to later bring it in and reveal it, so that it should be able to be in our world.

blocks.text:
This is the *nimshal* (what an analogy stands for) of everything said in chapter 12 about the *tzimtzum* (contraction) and the *reshimu* (the impression left after the tzimtzum). In G-dliness it is understood about the *tzimtzum* that is called the *makom panui* (the empty place).

What does "the empty place" mean? An empty place is somewhere you could put something. So the *tzimtzum* of the *makom panui* is the first *tzimtzum*, the one through which G-d allowed something that appears separate from Him, an outside existence, to exist. He made a place where you could put our world. And the point of it is that G-d hides His essential light **in order to be able to later bring it in and reveal it**, so that it should be able to be in our world.

phrases.en: But it's not that it's completely hidden.

phrases.he: אלא כמשל הסתלקות והעלם בעצמו, הידיעה של כל העומק והאריכות כששונה דרך קיצור כנ"ל
phrases.en: G-d's light is not completely hidden; it's like a teacher that when he's explaining it simply, he doesn't forget everything that he knew.

blocks.text: It is like what was said about the teacher. He just wants the student to understand, so he puts aside the whole deep explanation and feeds it to him slowly, so that eventually the student is able to get everything. **But it's not that it's completely hidden.** G-d's light is not completely hidden either: it is like a teacher who, when he explains something simply, does not forget everything that he knew.

The same when G-d creates the world. G-d created this table; so what happened to G-d? "Look, it's a table." You say, "No, G-d didn't become a table," right? G-d does not lose His ability by dealing with our world.

phrases.en: If so,

phrases.he: גם אחר כל ההשתלשלות דאבי''ע שעומד במקום פנוי זה,
phrases.en: even after the whole *hishtalshelus* to create the four worlds that stand in this empty place,

phrases.he: הרי בחינת העלם אור העצמות מקיף וסובב לכל השתלשלות דקו
phrases.en: the essence, the *Atzmus Ein Sof*, G-d's essential self-revelation, which means the revelation of G-d exactly the way He is, is still there.

phrases.he: וכמו שהיה אור העצמות קודם הצמצום ממלא את כל החלל ריקן ומקום פנוי הזה
phrases.en: And just like the light of G-d's essence, the revelation of G-d, before the *tzimtzum* filled this place,
so too after the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: הרי ישנו לאור העצמיות כמו שהוא בבחינת אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: G-d's light is still completely infinite; there's still a completely infinite revelation of G-d exactly the way He is,

phrases.he: רק שלא נגלה למטה לגבי שפע המקבלים
phrases.en: just that we're not seeing.

phrases.he: אבל לגבי עצמותו אין שינוי בזה כלל
phrases.en: But G-d still sees everything else, and there's no change to Him.

phrases.he: וכמו משל היודע כל האריכות להשיב לשואלו מיד, גם בשעה ששונה לתלמידו בקיצור כו'.
phrases.en: Like somebody that knows the whole *pilpul* of the Gemara: even when he's explaining it simply, in short, if you ask him a question, he'll right away tell you the whole thing.

blocks.text: **If so, even after the whole hishtalshelus** (the chain of descent) that makes the four worlds standing in this empty place, the *Atzmus Ein Sof* (G-d's essence), G-d's essential self-revelation, meaning the revelation of G-d exactly the way He is, **is still there.** It has not gone somewhere else; it is still here.

It is just that we are not seeing it; it is hidden. People say they want to see G-d, or they ask, "Can you see G-d?" The real truth is that you can't not see G-d. It's impossible for you not to see G-d. Wherever you look, and not only seeing: whatever you experience, you are experiencing the *Atzmus Ein Sof*, the essence of G-d. You just don't appreciate what you're seeing. It's really there.

Before the *tzimtzum* the light of G-d's essence, the revelation of G-d, filled this place, as it says in *Etz Chaim*, and G-d hid the light to make it look like our world. **So too after the tzimtzum**, G-d's light is still completely infinite: there is still a completely infinite revelation of G-d exactly the way He is, **just that we're not seeing.** G-d still knows that He can do everything, and He knows everything that He could do.

Just because He chose to make this one world does not mean that He can't make another world. Just because He is using these ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes) does not mean that He couldn't use another ten *sefiros*, or another thirty, or things we have no idea of that aren't even *sefiros*. Really there are infinite *sefiros* and infinite worlds and infinite everything, and G-d still has that ability and still knows everything that He could do. That is all still revealed to Him. He only revealed to us one of the possibilities.

**But G-d still sees everything else, and there's no change to Him.** It is like somebody who knows the whole *pilpul* (Talmudic debate) of the Gemara: even when he is explaining it simply, in short, if you ask him a question he will right away tell you the whole thing. So too, if we would *daven* (pray), G-d could right away reveal to us whatever we needed revealed. If He would want to, He could show you everything.

phrases.en: This that it says, this is *Tehillim* chapter 19, that G-d makes darkness His concealment,
like it says in the Gemara,
at the beginning there's darkness and afterwards there's light.
This darkness is only for us, but not to G-d.

phrases.he: שנמשך רק מבחינת הרשימו שנשאר אחר ההעלם כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: For us we only get the light out of the *reshimu*, which is darkness, and we have to pull out the light.

blocks.text: As for what it says, that **G-d makes darkness His concealment** (he gives it as *Tehillim* chapter 19), and the saying of the Sages, "First darkness and then light": the Gemara asks why the goats walk ahead of the lambs. The goats are usually black and the lambs are usually white. The answer is that this is the way the world works: **at the beginning there's darkness and afterwards there's light.**

blocks.question: Why does evil start out on the top, and only afterwards is there good?
blocks.text: That is the real question. And this is the way G-d made the world: at first He made a *tzimtzum*, and there is darkness, and only afterwards does He reveal the light.

blocks.title: The puzzle
blocks.text: The whole point of our world is like a puzzle. You hide the answer and it looks impossible, and then you think in a new, different way and you pull out the answer. Our world is the same: everything around us is really a revelation of G-d, but it looks to us as if it is completely hidden, and we have to pull it out.

**This darkness is only for us, but not to G-d.** G-d still sees the answer to the puzzle, the solution to the problem. For us, because it is drawn only from the *reshimu* that is left after the hiding, we get the light only out of the *reshimu*, which is darkness, and we have to pull the light out.

phrases.he: וזהו אתה קדוש ושמך, אור העצמי, קדוש ומובדל
phrases.en: This is what it means that You are holy and Your name is holy.
that You are He before He created the world, and You are He after He created the world.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אני יהו״ה לא שניתי כו'
phrases.en: I am G-d, I do not change.
why is it the same?
this that G-d reveals deep things from the darkness,
and the concealment,
out from this *reshimu*, out from this concealment, G-d reveals the *hishtalshelus* to us in the *Kav*,

phrases.he: הוא דווקא מאותו אור העצמות שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: That revelation is really the original light from before the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.text: This is what it means: **You are holy and Your name is holy.** G-d's essence stays above the whole *hishtalshelus* and is not affected by it; and even His name, even His light, stays holy and removed. It is not affected by the *tzimtzum*: it is still revealed, still existing in its full, original state, to G-d. Right now we are speaking from G-d's point of view, and from G-d's point of view the *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto* (literal).

**You are He before He created the world, and You are He after He created the world.** *Ata* (you) is the second person: you say "you" when somebody is here. *Hu* (he) is the third person. You are He: *ata* is the revelation and *hu* is the concealment. So we are saying that the revelation of Your essence is the same before the *tzimtzum* and after it.

Before the *tzimtzum*, the revelation of infinite light was a revelation of G-d's essence; so too now that G-d has created the world, the revelation that we see is also a revelation of G-d's essence. It is also "You are He after He created the world." As it says, **I am G-d, I do not change.** The *Ani* (I) also represents the idea of *Malchus* (kingship): the revelation of G-d does not change. Even though we now see it as different, it is still the revelation of G-d's essence, still the same revelation of Him.

Why is it the same? Because what G-d reveals afterwards **from the darkness**, and from the concealment, in the shining of the *Kav* (the ray of light): out of this *reshimu*, out of this concealment, G-d reveals the *hishtalshelus* to us in the *Kav*, and that is specifically from the same light of the Essence that was before the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.title: The Gemara pulled out of the Mishna
blocks.text:
**That revelation is really the original light from before the tzimtzum**, like the Gemara that we pull out of the Mishna. The Gemara we reconstitute from the Mishna is the same Gemara that they had; the Mishna was set up so that they could reconstitute whatever they forgot. But it is the original *sechel* (intellect). It did not change just because we are now pulling it out of the Mishna; it is still the same Gemara.

So too, even though we perceive G-d only through this world, when we look into the world and find G-dliness in it, we are getting the same revelation of G-dliness that there was before the *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: Not a makif on a pnimi: the Essence is not defined by our world
sections.summary: The light of the Essence around the chain is not a *makif* on a *pnimi*, the way the general *makif* of the *Kav* surrounds the four worlds; it is not even in the category of a light that is given. Like a person's taste, it affects everything without relating to any one thing: our world expresses G-d, but G-d cannot be defined by our world.

phrases.he: ואמנם לא נקרא אור העצמות שמקיף ההשתלשלות שבמקום פנוי כו', כמו בחינת מקיף לפנימי,
phrases.en: But nevertheless, even though the light that comes out in our *hishtalshelus* is coming from the revelation of G-d, we don't say that the light of G-d's essence is like a *makif* for the *hishtalshelus* in a way of *makif l'pnimi*.

phrases.he: כמקיף הכללי דקו שמקיף לאבי''ע בשוה כו'
phrases.en: unlike the general *makif* of the *Kav*, which surrounds *ABYA* equally, which is a *makif* on the *pnimi*.

blocks.text: Even so, though the light that comes out in our *hishtalshelus* is coming from the revelation of G-d, we do not say that the light of G-d's essence is a *makif* (encompassing light) for the *hishtalshelus* in the way of a *makif l'pnimi*, a *makif* on something inner.

blocks.title: Ice cream, a light bulb, a movie camera
blocks.text: The idea of a *makif l'pnimi* will be explained later. It is like a person who wants something specific, a person who wants ice cream. That desire is a general desire that includes all the particular things he is going to have to do to get what he wants. But it already relates specifically to a certain goal, so it is already somewhat defined by that goal. Or like a light bulb: it is meant specifically to give off light, so it is built specially to be something that gives off light. Or a movie camera: the lens is built to be transparent; it is built for a specific purpose.

blocks.title: A person's taste
blocks.text: Here it is different. This is not a *makif* on a *pnimi*; as will be explained later, it is like a person's taste. A person's taste affects everything he does. When he is getting his ice cream he will pick a certain flavor according to his taste, and it affects everything, even what kind of cone he will want. If he is building a house, it decides exactly how he wants everything, down to the bathroom drapes. But it does not relate to any one detail more than any other detail; it relates to anything he will do.

blocks.title: The house and the sky
blocks.text: So it surrounds it, it is *makif* on it, and it is the real cause, but it does not relate directly to it. Generally, a person's house is like a *makif* on a *pnimi*: it is built specifically to be his house, and he directs it, created it, controls it. The sky is like a *makif* that is not on a *pnimi*. In a way it is on a *pnimi*, but relatively it does not really relate directly to you: if it's going to rain, it's going to rain. A *makif* on a *pnimi* is connected to something already separate from the person, but it is already defined by that.

The *makif* that is not on a *pnimi*, which is what we are talking about, means that G-d can reveal Himself in anything, so it does not relate specifically to our world. It's just that if G-d is going to make our world, He is also revealed in our world. "You understand what I'm saying?" The light before the *tzimtzum* is not G-d's ability to make this world. It is a revelation of G-d exactly as He is. It is the idea of a *hiyuli* (raw potential): since it is a *hiyuli*, it could also come out as our world, and therefore our world expresses it.

But it is a one-way thing. You can't define G-d by our world, because it is not a *makif* on a *pnimi*. And yet our world is an expression of G-d, because G-d's light is *makif* on our world.

It is **unlike the general makif of the Kav**, which surrounds *ABYA* (the four worlds) equally; that one is a *makif* on the *pnimi*. The general *makif* after the *tzimtzum*, the *sovev kol almin* (the light that encompasses all worlds), is the revelation of G-dliness that relates to our world: the ten *sefiros*, G-d's ability to be a Creator, and all these things. The essence of G-dliness does not relate specifically to our world.

phrases.he: כי הרי עדיין אינו בגדר וסוג בחינת אור השפעה כלל,
phrases.en: because the essence, the light before the *tzimtzum*, G-d's self-revelation, doesn't relate at all to be something to be given over.

phrases.he: גם לא להיות בחינת מקיף כו'
phrases.en: You can't even call it like a general thing, like a *makif*.

phrases.he: רק אור העצמות, שהוא בחינת התגלותו כמו שהוא בעצמות
phrases.en: The light is just a revelation of G-d exactly as He is.

blocks.text: The reason is that the essence, the light before the *tzimtzum*, G-d's self-revelation, does not relate at all to being something to be given over. As was said about the power of movement, it does not have any particular movements in it, because it is not in the category and the realm of movement. **You can't even call it like a general thing, like a makif.**

It is only the light of the Essence, **just a revelation of G-d exactly as He is.** Just a revelation of Him. As was explained before about the *hiyuli*, it is just Him: "It's not coats, it's not shoes, it's not a power of movement, it's just Him."

phrases.en: therefore we say,
He endures
and His name endures,
yet we also say, blessed be He and blessed be His name.

phrases.he: רק מבחינת אותיות דגליף בטהירו עילאה זה,
phrases.en: The revelation of our world is coming only from what G-d estimated in the *tehiru ila'a*, in the *glif glifu*, in *Kadmon*,

phrases.he: שהוא מה ששיער בעצמו בכח כו'
phrases.en: which is what G-d estimated in potential, how He wants it to be.

phrases.he: וגם זה הוא הנשאר בבחינת העלם והסתלקות קצת
phrases.en: But even this estimation, even that that was estimated, the *tzimtzum* also hid that,

phrases.he: דהיינו רק לפי ערך אופן הנצרך להשתלשלות אחר צמצום זה
phrases.en: and it's only revealed according to what is needed for this *tzimtzum*, but it's not fully revealed,

blocks.text:
Therefore we say, **He endures and His name endures**: G-d and His name remain the same; enduring means that even after the *tzimtzum* they are still found. And we also say, **blessed be He and blessed be His name**, meaning that it is revealed within our *hishtalshelus*: the revelation of G-dliness is brought down, and G-d's essence is revealed here.

But the revelation in our world comes only from what G-d estimated in the *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity), in the *glif glifu* (the engraving), in *Kadmon*: what He estimated in potential, how He wants it to be. It is like what will be explained later about taste, that a person's taste influences every detail of what he does. That is the way it was estimated, the way He wants it to be; but it was not estimated specifically for this thing. "We'll talk about it later."

**But even this estimation**, what was estimated, the *tzimtzum* also hid. It is **only revealed according to what is needed for this tzimtzum**, not fully revealed, *v'dai l'mevin* (and this is enough for one who understands).

So this was the *nimshal* for the *mashal* of the teacher and the student. First, just as the teacher does not forget, G-d did not change or lose His ability, and He really still knows who He is. He didn't go, "Oh no, I'm a table!" "He's not like having an identity crisis or something." Second, just as the teacher sees the whole explanation of the Gemara in the Mishna, G-d sees the full revelation of His essence in the world. When G-d looks at the world, He sees how it is really a revelation of Him.

And that really means that if you know how to look into anything in the world, you will see the whole essence of G-d, infinite. Even something as small as a little thing, a table, a pear, whatever it is: look into it, study it, and you will find G-d there. And even as far as we are concerned, though to us it looks hidden because of the *reshimu*, we can pull out the whole light until we find the original light of G-d's essence, because it is really there. It is just hidden, and we have to work to pull it out. We don't appreciate what we're seeing; but we are seeing it.

blocks.title: The eye doctor's card
blocks.text:
Rabbi Walters used to go on *mivtzaim* (outreach) with an eye doctor who gave out a business card. On the back was a black and white picture, and it said, "What am I?" You look at it and you don't see anything. "Come on, don't you see? So simple, why don't you see it?" You look at it, turn it; you don't see anything. "First of all, you're holding it the wrong way," and he turns it for you. Still you don't see anything. "It's a cow." You look back at it, you try squinting and everything; you don't see a cow. "Here, let me show you." He starts pointing: "This is the eye, this is the ear, this is the nose, this is the body, it's the fence." And all of a sudden it clicks, and you see that it is actually a black and white photograph of a cow standing in a field.

Your mind did not register the image because of the way the things came together. But once you get it, once it clicks, for the rest of your life, whenever you see that picture, you'll right away see a cow.

That's the way it is with the world: the whole time you are seeing G-d; you just don't realize what you're seeing. It just doesn't click. And *Chassidus*, the Torah and all these *mitzvos*, making a *birur* (refinement), refining the sparks and everything: what is the idea? It is just to put it in order. You see what this is and what that is, and when you see how it all fits together, all of a sudden it clicks, "Oh!", and you realize that you are looking at G-d.

sections.title: The soul and the body: connected, yet not changed
sections.summary: By the second *mashal*, the soul's life in the body: the soul is bound to the body and affected by it, yet it loses nothing when a limb fails. So the light of the Essence shines after the *tzimtzum*, connected to the measured revelation of the *Kav*, and is not changed by it. All the *meshalim* come to one point.

phrases.he: וגם על פי אופן משל הב' הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: also according to the second *mashal*,
the consciousness of the soul that's in the body,

phrases.he: שמשתנה ממהות רוחני למהות גשמי כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that it changes from being spiritual in nature and essence to being physical,

phrases.he: גם כן אין זה שינוי כלל,
phrases.en: This is also not a real change,

phrases.he: שהרי כמו שיש קישור וחיבור לחיות הגשמי לחיות הרוחני
phrases.en: just like there is a bond and a connection between the physical consciousness and the spiritual consciousness,

phrases.he: ממה שרואים התפעלות הנפש ממקרי חיות הגוף,
phrases.en: like we see that the soul is affected by what happens to the body.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה לא ישתנה בעצם הרוחנית מחסרון התפשטות חיות אבר גשמי כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: And on the other hand, it's not affected if something happens to the physical body.

phrases.he: כך אין שינוי בבחינת אור העצמות, להיותו מאיר גם אחר הצמצום
phrases.en: So too, even when G-d shines, reveals Himself after the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: גם שאינו רק לפי ערך ההשתלשלות
phrases.en: and even though after the *tzimtzum* G-d reveals Himself in a way of *memalei*, individualized according to the proportion and the relationship of the *hishtalshelus*,
nevertheless, even though it's being revealed in a limited way after the *tzimtzum*, it's still connected to the *Atzmus* of the light before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה בצמצום האור בבחינת הקו,
phrases.en: even though it comes in a measured way,

phrases.he: אין זה שינוי כלל באור העצמות על פי משל זה
phrases.en: So there's no real change in the light of the *Atzmus*, based on this *mashal*.

blocks.text: So far we gave the *nimshal* for the first *mashal*, the teacher. Now comes the *nimshal* for the second *mashal*, the life of the soul and the body: **the consciousness of the soul that's in the body**, which **changes from being spiritual in nature and essence to being physical**.

**This is also not a real change.** The *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto*: that is the point being brought out. Based on that *mashal* we also understand that when G-d creates the world, it is not a real change in G-d. There is **a bond and a connection between the physical consciousness and the spiritual consciousness**: we see that the soul is affected by what happens to the body. The real consciousness in the body is the soul. That is what is really perceiving everything, and what gets happy and sad and everything, is the soul.

So on the one hand, the essence of the soul, as it is in its original state, connects to the body: it is revealed in the body, not fully, but it is connected to it. **And on the other hand, it's not affected if something happens to the physical body.** If the eye gets ruined, G-d forbid, and the body's power of sight is taken away, the soul does not lose its power of sight.

So too when G-d shines and reveals Himself after the *tzimtzum*. So I say, this table is revealing G-d; that does not mean that if I burn the table I am hurting G-d.

After the *tzimtzum* G-d reveals Himself in a way of *memalei* (filling), individualized according to the proportion and relationship of the *hishtalshelus*; even so, it is still connected to the *Atzmus* of the light before the *tzimtzum*. It comes in a measured way, and that means that there is *hispaalus* (being affected), so to speak: G-d answers our prayers; if something is holy it reveals G-d more, and the revelation can go away; giving life, measure for measure, all that kind of stuff, which is like *hispaalus*. But that is only the way it is after. **So there's no real change in the light of the Atzmus, based on this mashal.**

phrases.he: וכן על פי משל הג' מכח התנועה בגשם או כמשל התחכמות מכח המשכיל הנזכר לעיל

phrases.en: it all comes up to one general point,

blocks.text: So too by the third *mashal*, the power of movement in the body, or the intellect from the *koach hamaskil* (the power of insight): **it all comes up to one general point.** The *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto* from G-d's point of view: He is not lessened by making the world, and even within the world G-d sees a full revelation of Himself. And even from our point of view, there is really a full revelation of G-dliness in the world; we just don't appreciate what we're seeing. And when we pray, we are really asking from G-d Himself, and He is really the one that answers our prayers; everything, it is G-d Himself. And yet it is not a change. We understand that a little bit, and we will understand it better from other things to be discussed later.

sections.title: The reshimu is the power of limitation in the unlimited light
sections.summary: The *reshimu*, compared above to the short version that includes the whole length, is in G-dliness the *koach hahagbala*: the power of the unlimited light to bring all of itself, limited, into one impression, even into a speck of dust. G-d can do anything, and so He can also limit.

phrases.en: the *reshimu* that was explained previously,

phrases.he: שזהו כמו הקיצור שכלול בו כל האריכות
phrases.en: which is like the summary that includes the whole *arichus*, like the way the Mishna includes the Gemara,

phrases.he: הנה למעלה יובן מזה שזהו בחינת כח ההגבלה שיש באור אין סוף הבלתי מוגבל בעצם
phrases.en: But *reshimu* in the *nimshal* is the power of limitation that exists in the *Or Ein Sof*, which is essentially not limited.

phrases.he: דהיינו להביא כל הארות אור העצמות הבלתי גבול בבחינת הגבול
phrases.en: In other words, the power of the light is to reveal G-d; the power of the *reshimu* is to reveal G-d in a limited way.
that's the idea of the impression,

phrases.he: שכולל בבחינת הגבלה מבחינת כל עצמות אור אין סוף,
phrases.en: that it includes in a limited way the whole *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*,
like the *kitzur* that includes everything, like the way the Mishna includes the Gemara.

blocks.text: So now comes the *nimshal* for the *reshimu*: **the reshimu that was explained previously**, which is like the summary that includes the whole length, **like the way the Mishna includes the Gemara**.

In the *nimshal*, the *reshimu* is the *koach hahagbala*, the power of limitation that exists in the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light), which in its essence is not limited. **The power of the light is to reveal G-d; the power of the reshimu is to reveal G-d in a limited way**: to bring the entire revelation of G-d exactly the way He is, the whole light of the *Ein Sof*, to be revealed in some infinitely little speck of dust on this table, so that the whole *gilui* (revelation) of the Essence is in that speck of dust. G-d could do that, right? That is the power of limitation.

**That's the idea of the impression**: it includes in a limited way the whole *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*, like the *kitzur* (shortening) that includes everything, the way the Mishna includes the Gemara. It is very short, but it is in there. So really anything in the world, even though you say it is so small, G-d packs the whole *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* into it. And if you were able to study anything in the world properly, even the tiniest little particle, you would be able to find the whole *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* in it.

phrases.en: because G-d can do anything; He's omnipotent,

phrases.he: וכלול בו גם כן מכח המגביל
phrases.en: He also has the power to limit.

phrases.he: להגביל ולכלול ברשימה א' מכל אור העצמות כו'
phrases.en: So He also has the power to limit and to include in a single impression, in a single point, all the light of the *Atzmus*.

blocks.text: **Because G-d can do anything; He's omnipotent,** He also has the power to limit. And if G-d is going to limit, He can do a really good job: He can take even something infinite and bring it down and reveal it in an infinitely limited, infinitesimal way. So He also has the power to limit and to include in a single impression, in a single point, all the light of the *Atzmus*, as explained elsewhere at length. That is the main *nimshal*.

But as was said before, the *mashal* of the *kitzur*, the Mishna, is not really a good *mashal* for the *reshimu*; it does not get the point across. So now it will be explained, based on the other *meshalim* (analogies), that in the *nimshal* it is really more limited than that. It is not just that G-d could make it very dense, but even more than that.

sections.title: Truer likenesses: the craftsman's mark, the mnemonic, the thrown stone, the hint
sections.summary: The *reshimu* means that everything was taken away, like a footprint when the foot is gone, so the short version is not a true likeness. Truer are the craftsman's line, the mnemonic, and most of all the thrown stone, whose force is hidden in it and in the arm, and the hand's sign or the writing that hides an idea: the world looks separate and self-running, and G-d's involvement is hidden in it.

phrases.he: אך הנה באמת אין זה דמיון אמיתי לבחינת הרשימו הנשאר בחלל ריקן ומקום פנוי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: This *mashal*, this comparison to the *kitzur*, is not the proper comparison for the *reshimu* that's left over in this empty place.

phrases.he: כי הוא מורה שנסתלק משם הכל
phrases.en: because the idea of the *reshimu* indicates that everything was removed; that doesn't mean that it was just made very condensed, it means that it's not there.

phrases.he: ולא שנשאר איזה אור רק שהוא בקצור וגבול,
phrases.en: and not that there was some light left, there's a little bit of a revelation, it's just very condensed,

phrases.he: אלא רק בחינת רשימו בעלמא כו'
phrases.en: but only an impression, meaning that the original thing was taken away, like a footprint; the foot's gone.

blocks.text: The comparison to the *kitzur* is not the proper comparison for the *reshimu* that is left over in this empty place, because the idea of the *reshimu* indicates that everything was removed. That does not mean it was just made very condensed; it means that it's not there. Not that some light was left, a little bit of a revelation, just very condensed, but only an impression, meaning that the original thing was taken away. Like a footprint: **the foot's gone.**

phrases.he: אם כן הדמיון האמיתי הוא מרושם וציון קו קצר שעושין האומנין, שכולל כל אריכות מעשה הבנין
phrases.en: So if so, a better *mashal* is like the little blueprint or the little notes that a craftsman makes for how to build the entire thing,
even more than this,
like a mnemonic,
so too in G-dliness,

phrases.he: כתיב זכר רב טובך, העצמי כו'
phrases.en: that our world is only like a *zecher*, is only like a remembrance of G-d's abundant goodness.
and the like.

blocks.title: The craftsman's notes
blocks.text: So the true likeness is **the little blueprint or the little notes that a craftsman makes for how to build the entire thing.** There is no explanation there. In the Mishna there is an explanation of the Gemara; here there is no explanation, it is just some line. But from that you can really know how to build the whole thing.

And **even more than this**: it is like a mnemonic, where it is completely hidden. And **so too in G-dliness**, it is written, "Remember Your abundant goodness": our world is only like a remembrance of G-d's abundant goodness. It is only like the letters of a mnemonic, **and the like.**

The idea is that the *reshimu* means that G-d makes the world in a way that His light is completely hidden. There is no actual revelation of G-d, and that is why we don't see G-d. Naturally, a person feels that he is seeing a physical world; he does not feel that he is seeing G-d, because G-d completely hid. His revelation does not come directly. It is revealed only like a mnemonic, or a blueprint, a foreign thing that hints at it. So when we see a table, the fact that it was created hints to us that there is a Creator. But we don't see the Creator; we see a hint of Him.

phrases.he: ויותר בהעלם והסתלקות הוא כמשל הזורק אבן כו' כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Or even more so is like the *mashal* of throwing a stone, which is the main *mashal* of the *reshimu*.
like it says in *Sefer HaBahir*,
like it was thrown.

phrases.he: שהרי בחינת הרשימו נשאר נבדל בריחוק מקום מעצמות האור וכו'
phrases.en: because the *reshimu* is left so that it seems like it's distant from the *Atzmus HaOr*,
And the power that's hidden within this *reshimu* is called

phrases.he: בחינת העלם אור, נבדל מהעלם עצמות האור דאין סוף
phrases.en: the concealment of the light, which is separate from the essential concealment of the light of the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: כמו כח נבדל הנעלם בזריקת אבן
phrases.en: Like when you throw a stone: there's a power of movement, there's a force that's hidden now within the stone,

phrases.he: שבא מכח היד שכבר נעלם בעצמו כו'
phrases.en: And also in the person's arm that threw it, you don't see the implementation of his force.

blocks.text: **Or even more so** it is like the *mashal* of throwing a stone, which is the main *mashal* of the *reshimu*. So it says in *Sefer HaBahir*, **like it was thrown.** The *reshimu* is left so that it seems distant from the Essence of the light, and that is like our world: our world looks as if it was thrown, so that we don't see G-d's involvement so much.

This is not how it actually is. But it looks to us as if we could look at the world as something that was just thrown, as if G-d made it a one-time thing and now it is just going on its own. Like there was a big bang, and it sent everything flying, and now it's going. In general, the physical world looks thrown: it looks as if it totally left the realm of G-dliness and is a totally separate thing. The whole look of a natural system makes it look independent.

The power hidden within this *reshimu* is called **the concealment of the light, which is separate from the essential concealment of the light of the Ein Sof.** What does that mean? It is like the separate power hidden in a thrown stone, which came from the power of the hand that is already hidden in itself. When you throw a stone there is a power of movement, a force that is now hidden within the stone. You don't see the force being applied to the stone; you just see its effect, that the stone is moving. **And also in the person's arm that threw it, you don't see the implementation of his force**: you just see his arm at rest. So it went and was hidden again: his movement is hidden in his arm, and it is hidden in the stone.

Why does it say "the concealment of the light, separate from the concealment of the Essence"? Because there is the way it is hidden in the stone, and there is the way it is hidden in the arm. It is hidden in two ways: it is hidden within the world, and G-d's involvement is hidden too, so that we don't see G-d revealing His power directly. It looks as if He is just sitting back and watching, and the world is going on its own. Unless there are miracles, we don't see, so to speak, G-d's hand involved with the world.

That the world can look like a separate thing, just going in a system, is the main thing of the *tzimtzum*: that G-d is hidden, that He looks uninvolved. And that makes us feel that we are independent from G-d.

phrases.en: like all the orbits and stars, or the planets and the stars,
that are moving from G-d's power of movement,

phrases.he: הנעלם, שבא בבחינת זריקה מאור וכח האלה״י
phrases.en: which is hidden within them, from G-d's power of throwing,
the *chitzoniyus* nine *kelim* of *Malchus d'Asiya*,

phrases.he: שנקרא זה כח הנבדל בחינת מלכות שבמלכות
phrases.en: once they're actually thrown, that is called *Malchus sheb'Malchus*,
which *Malchus sheb'Malchus* is where it becomes far from you,

phrases.he: ולא כמו הכתיבה באצבע או כח יד הפועל עצמו בנפעל
phrases.en: and not like when you're writing or when you're moving something with your hand,
when you're actually moving something directly with your hand, that's the revelation of your power in a way that's close, that you see the connection.
That's just plain *Malchus*.

blocks.text: So too all the *galgalim* (the celestial orbits), the planets and the stars, which move from G-d's power of movement hidden within them, from G-d's power of throwing: G-d actually made them start moving. That power is **the chitzoniyus nine kelim** (the outer nine vessels) **of Malchus d'Asiya**, which set the whole universe moving; specifically, the nine planets correspond to the nine *kelim*.

Once they are actually thrown, that separate power is called *Malchus sheb'Malchus*. The power of movement, the way it is still connected, is the first nine *sefiros* of *Malchus*. When you are holding something in your hand and moving it, that is the first, plain *Malchus*, the first nine *sefiros*. When you throw it and it becomes separate from your power, that is *Malchus sheb'Malchus*.

All these levels really exist; it is a question of what you are perceiving. When you look into things and realize how really every moment G-d is controlling and moving the world and the planets, that is a revelation of the nine *sefiros* of *Malchus*: if a person would investigate and realize that really every single moment the planets need to be moved by G-d. When a person looks at them as if they were just thrown, on their own, "and maybe G-d threw it, you know, once upon a time, but now, you know, Big Bang and then it's just going," that is *Malchus sheb'Malchus*. It looks like it was just set flying.

That is the idea of a *reshimu*: you don't see G-d's involvement directly, but since He did it, you can look into it and find a hint about Him, "like graphology or something." *Malchus sheb'Malchus* **is where it becomes far from you**, not like writing or moving something with your hand. When you are actually moving something directly with your hand, that is the revelation of your power in a way that is close: you see the connection. **That's just plain Malchus**, as explained elsewhere at length.

On the text he remarks that there should probably be another parenthesis after "as explained elsewhere at length", or else the opening parenthesis before it should not be there.

phrases.en: and *meshalim* that are even closer for this, the idea of the *reshimu*,
like a hint with a hand motion for a *sechel*.
The movement lifting those two fingers hints at a whole thing, but the *sechel* is completely hidden there.

phrases.he: שזהו נקרא בחינת הלבשה ותפיסא בדבר נבדל כו'
phrases.en: That is the idea that it changes its *mahus*: it's being represented by something, it's enclothed in something different, and it's being expressed by that.

phrases.he: וכן כשכותב שכל וחכמה בתנועת האצבע כו'
phrases.en: Same thing when you're writing: there the intellect goes through the hand, and it's hidden, but then it comes out through being on paper.

blocks.title: The peace sign
blocks.text: *Meshalim* even closer to the idea of the *reshimu*: **a hint with a hand motion for a sechel**, where the idea is hidden in the physical movement. Like a peace sign, right? The movement of lifting those two fingers hints at a whole thing, but the *sechel* is completely hidden there. A person looks at it and does not see intellect; he just sees a movement.

The same thing: we look and just see a physical world. We don't see meaning. You say, "Yeah, that's because you don't understand the language, you don't understand what's going on. You don't understand what it's supposed to represent." It is true that you are seeing a physical thing, you are seeing fingers; or in the *nimshal*, you are seeing the trees and the tables and everything in the sky. "Well, I don't see G-d." "Yeah, that's because you don't understand how this is a symbol for what this represents."

This is called being enclothed and grasped in a separate thing: **it changes its mahus** (what a thing is in itself). It is being represented by something, it is enclothed in something different, and it is being expressed by that.

blocks.title: G-d writing His autobiography
blocks.text: **Same thing when you're writing**: the intellect goes through the hand and is hidden, but then it comes out on paper. In the same way, even though here it is just physical movement and physical things, it is like a language: G-d is like writing, as He is writing His autobiography. And all the different changes that we see in the world are like the changes on the paper.

That is how the revelation can come out of the *reshimu* again: when you look and see the differences between everything, it reveals it again. At first it is just hidden as a physical movement, but really there is an intellect there. The *reshimu* is like the written thing, or the movement of the hand, where the intellect is completely hidden.

If you look at the world at the simplest face value, see it as something separate, and look at everything individually as objects with no connection to anything else, then you don't see any meaning. But as the next chapter explains, when you start to look at the picture of how they all fit together, you see that there is a language; even though if you look at each letter on the paper, you won't be able to figure out any meaning. "We'll talk about that next chapter."

phrases.he: כך למעלה, בחינת הרשימו בחינת דבר נבדל בערך,
phrases.en: so too, *reshimu* is the idea that reality seems like something that's separate from G-dliness.

phrases.he: שבו מלובש בהעלם מכללות אור העצמות כו'
phrases.en: but nevertheless, really the whole light of G-d is hidden within our world, and if we'll look into it, we'll be able to find it.

blocks.text: So too above: the *reshimu* is the idea that **reality seems like something that's separate from G-dliness.** The way we perceive reality, a physical created world, is as something separate. The table as we know it is not G-d; it is a table. "That's the whole thing of *avoda zara*" (idol worship): the world as we know it, we say, what, that's not G-d, this is a world, right?

And G-d's involvement in it is also hidden. So it is both: G-d is being revealed through something that seems separate from Him, and it is also like a change of *mahus*, from a spiritual thing to a physical thing, from a G-dly, infinite thing to a physical, limited thing. **But nevertheless, really the whole light of G-d is hidden within our world, and if we'll look into it, we'll be able to find it.** "And that's what we're going to try to do."

sections.title: Everything comes from the reshimu: nothing is missing from You
sections.summary: Though everything was removed and the light remains in the *reshimu* only hidden, short and hinted, or as a thrown, separate power, all the details of the *Kav* come from it, because it includes everything. It holds what G-d estimated in *Kadmon*, seen in one glance; so all that is formed is not missing "from You".

phrases.en: however, from all of these *meshalim* together,

phrases.he: יובן על כל פנים כללות ענין הרשימו
phrases.en: it's at least understood, the general *inyan* of the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: דגם שהוא בא בבחינת הסתלקות הכל,
phrases.en: that even though the *reshimu* comes in a way where everything is removed,

phrases.he: ולא נשאר בה רק בהעלם גדול
phrases.en: the original light only remains in the *reshimu* in a very hidden way,
it's completely short and just hinted at,
or it can also be looked at in a little bit different way: it's like something that was thrown, that it's now seen as something that's separate and outside from the self.
nevertheless,

phrases.he: מזה עצמו בא ונמשך כל פרטי ההשתלשלות דקו
phrases.en: from this itself, from this *reshimu* itself, comes all the details of what comes on into the *Kav*, through the *Kav*.
it all comes from this *reshimu*.
because in this little impression,

phrases.he: להיותה כוללת הכל בהעלם על כל פנים,
phrases.en: since it includes everything, albeit in a very hidden way,

phrases.he: היא הנותנת שיוכל לבא הכל בהתגלות על ידי בחינת הקו
phrases.en: this is what gives the possibility that everything should be able to come out from it, should be revealed from it through the *Kav*,
everything in *hishtalshelus* until the end of *Asiya*, the physical world.

blocks.text: We just finished explaining the *nimshal* for each of the *meshalim* of the *reshimu*; now comes the general idea of its *nimshal*. From all of these *meshalim* together **it's at least understood, the general inyan** (concept) of the *reshimu*. What is it? Even though the *reshimu* comes in a way where everything is removed, and the original light only remains in it in a very hidden way, **it's completely short and just hinted at.** Or it can also be looked at in a little different way: it is like something that was thrown, so that it is now seen as something separate and outside the self.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 33 opens by summing up the meshalim of lines 34-53 before it reads line 54.

blocks.text: **Nevertheless**, even though the original light in it is so hidden and so short, from this itself, from the *reshimu* itself, come all the details of what comes into the *Kav*, through the *Kav*. **It all comes from this reshimu.**

Because this little impression includes everything, albeit in a very hidden way, it is what gives the possibility that everything can come out of it and be revealed from it through the *Kav*. It is true that everything is very hidden there, but since it is all there, at least it is there; and once it is there, it can already be pulled out by the *Kav*. Exactly how that is possible will be explained in the next chapter, because it seems that it should be very hard or impossible to do. But once it is there, it is possible to take it back out.

If it were not there at all, it would be *tzimtzum kipshuto*: it would be completely hidden and would not come out. There are certain things that do not come out of the *reshimu*, other *sefiros* and things. Really they are hidden there too, so really they could come out; but the main thing in the *reshimu* is what was estimated in *Kadmon* of what is going to be in the *hishtalshelus*. Even that is hidden; and in a deeper way the whole light of the Essence is hidden there too, and from that you can pull out anything. So this is pulled out through the *Kav* to the end of *Asiya* (the world of Action): **everything in hishtalshelus until the end of Asiya, the physical world.**

phrases.he: וכמאמר כל היצור לא נכחד ממך
phrases.en: like it says that all of what is created, or really *yetzur* means what is formed, is not missing from You.
from You, *davka*, meaning from G-d Himself.

phrases.he: שזהו הכל נעשה ונמשך בגלוי כמו שעלה ברצונו הפשוט בעצמות האור שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: that everything in the *hishtalshelus* is done according to, is made and is brought out according to the way that it arose in G-d's simple will within Himself,
in the estimation that He made in the light before the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: שהרי במחשבה קדומה זו ששיער בעצמו
phrases.en: because in this original thought where He estimated it to Himself, and this we mean *Kadmon* here,

phrases.he: הוא צופה ומביט הכל בסקירה א'
phrases.en: He saw everything from the beginning to the end in one glance.

phrases.he: דהיינו מה שנסקר בהעלם ובקיצור ורמז ברשימו זו כו'
phrases.en: And this whole estimation is what's put into this impression, this *reshimu*, and in this *reshimu*, everything is seen in a hidden and in a very short and hinted way, in one glance.

blocks.text: As it says, all that is created is not missing from You; really *yetzur* means what is formed. **From You, davka** (specifically): from G-d Himself. That means that everything that comes out in the world comes from G-d Himself.

Everything in the *hishtalshelus* is made and brought out according to the way it arose in G-d's simple will within Himself, **in the estimation that He made in the light before the tzimtzum**, in *Kadmon*. For in this original thought where He estimated it to Himself, and this is what *Kadmon* means here, **He saw everything from the beginning to the end in one glance.** It includes everything.

And this whole estimation is what is put into the impression, the *reshimu*, and in the *reshimu* everything is seen in a hidden, very short and hinted way, in one glance. It's all there. So even though it is like one point, hidden in it is really everything.

sections.title: The craftsman's blueprint: a plan kept so that the work is ours
sections.summary: The craftsman builds the whole house from his outline, which he makes so that he will not deviate or have to think it through again. G-d does not forget; turning the *mashal* around, He makes the world look like a fixed system He set up once, so that the *avoda* falls on us and we feel the responsibility.

from its beginning to its end.

blocks.title: The craftsman's blueprint
blocks.text: This is like **the analogy of the craftsman's blueprint**: specifically from looking at the blueprint, the craftsman knows how to make everything. He can build the whole house from the blueprint, with all of its most minute details, **from its beginning to its end.**

So why does he make the blueprint? To look at a blueprint and understand everything, you already have to know about a lot of things, and the only one who really appreciates the blueprint completely is the one who made it, especially if it is not a standardized blueprint. The *roshem* (outline) of a craftsman does not have to be a regular blueprint; it could be just his personal little notes that only he understands. So why did he make it? **He makes it so that he will not forget the whole reason of why he decided to do it exactly this way**, when he is in the middle of building the building.

**So that he shouldn't deviate from it, and he won't have to go think about it again.** In the middle of building he gets involved in thinking about how to build it, and he forgets: "Oh, why didn't I want... There's a reason why I wanted to put this here and not there. Cuz now it seems like, oh, it's better to put it there. Why did I want to put it here?" And then he has to go rethinking the whole thing, why structurally it won't work to put it there, or, "Oh yeah, I forgot, they have to run the plumbing through that way." There's a reason why.

If you want to be an architect: somebody was just telling Rabbi Walters that he wants to be an architect, and that besides the engineering, to make sure a building is structurally sound, they have to study plumbing, to know how to make room for the pipes to go through, and electricity, and all these different considerations. They have to understand how these work to know how to take them into consideration. But he does not want to have to think about those things while he is building the building. He just wants to think about how to build it.

phrases.he: וכמו כן ענין הציונים ללימוד עמוק שבעצמו כו'
phrases.en: so too the idea of making little notes, sort of mnemonics, to help you remember a deep subject,

phrases.he: שזהו תועלת לידע מהם כל אורך עיון עומק עצמותו שיש לו, פן ינטה ממנו כו'
phrases.en: and from remembering that, it will remind you the whole *halacha* with all the reasons and everything, and you won't deviate from it.

blocks.title: Notes for a deep subject
blocks.text: **So too the idea of making little notes, sort of mnemonics, to help you remember a deep subject.** If you want to remember the *halacha* (the law), and you went through a whole *pilpul* to finally figure it out, then you just remember a short little thing, like the idea of the Mishna, or even shorter, like a mnemonic. And from remembering that, it will remind you of the whole *halacha*, with all the reasons and everything, **and you won't deviate from it.**

The general *nimshal* is that when G-d estimated to Himself on the level of *Kadmon*, He estimated everything that is going to be in the world, as it says, all that is formed is not missing from You. Everything that is going to be in the whole history of the world, with all the details, down to exactly how many hairs are going to be on each person's head, how many feathers every bird is going to have, how many times every blade of grass is going to shake back and forth in the wind: all of that was planned out, and it all needs to be exactly that way for *Moshiach* to come. That is part of *hashgacha pratis* (divine providence): the world *davka* has to be this way. There is a certain special thing about it, that G-d likes it this way. And now it is just like looking at the blueprint and bringing out what was already planned.

blocks.question: Why would the *mashal* of the blueprint apply to G-d, who is not going to forget or deviate? Why would He need the *reshimu*?
blocks.text:
Whenever you look at the *mashal* and the *nimshal*, you always have to fix it, and here there is a difference between them. In the *mashal*, the craftsman needs to make the blueprint so that he won't forget, because he might make a mistake, or just so that he won't have to think about it: two points, that he doesn't want to have to rethink it, and that he doesn't want to deviate. But G-d is not going to go, "Oh, what was it again?" He is not going to make a mistake, "Oh, I forgot, yeah."

Of course the answer is that He does not need the *reshimu*, and He is not going to forget. Anytime you go from the *mashal* to the *nimshal* you have to switch it around: take the deficiencies that apply to the *mashal* and put them on us. G-d wants to make it look as if the world is able to run on its own without His having to be constantly involved.

He wants to make it look like a one-time involvement: He figured it all out, and now it is able to go on its own. As long as you are working down from the level of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation), you still see G-d as involved, but as involved without really reaching into His essence, without any real new creative thing coming from Him. You just see Him as following the system He set up. So there are two things G-d wants it to look like to us: that He is not going back into the *omek* (depth), and that He is not going to deviate from it, that it is like a system.
And the reason that He wants these two things is that He wants to put the *avoda* (divine service) on us: to make it that we should feel that G-d set up the world a certain way.

blocks.title: The Rebbe Rashab's oath
blocks.text:
There is a story, they say, that the Rebbe Rashab made G-d swear that He would not change the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chain of descending worlds) when the *bochurim* (young yeshiva students) understand it wrong, to make them right. When they are learning *Chassidus* and misunderstand the *hishtalshelus*, G-d could just make them right; He could change the *hishtalshelus*. So the Rebbe Rashab made Him swear that He would not change it, so that they would have to work to understand it right.

That is the thing about the *reshimu*, "lest he deviate from it": that He should not change from it.

G-d makes a commitment, so to speak, with Himself that He is going to run the world in a certain way. And by not changing from it, He gives us the thing we have to do, the *avoda*, and makes it important that we do things *davka* this way and not another way: He wants *Moshiach* to come like this, and He is not going to let us off without accomplishing that particular goal. That is one of the things that makes it hard.

He also wants to make it look as if it is not coming every moment from His *etzem* (essence) anymore. If you would see how it is always coming straight from G-d's choice, it would not look like a system. It would look as if every moment G-d is just deciding what He wants to do.

blocks.title: The teacher's class plan
blocks.text: Like a teacher in a classroom who makes a system for punishment and reward, for how to mark the grades, what the class requirements are. He plans it out beforehand, a class plan: now we have to accomplish these things, and if you don't accomplish these things, you're not going to pass. And he wants it to look as if that is something outside of him as a teacher, and he is just working within that framework. Otherwise you don't feel that there is a weight on you. You just feel, "Oh, he's just doing whatever he wants," and so you can just ask him to be nice and to change it.

So really, when we *daven*, we do: we ask G-d to be nice and to change it, and sometimes He changes it for us. But unless we go past this level, G-d, by setting up this *tzimtzum*, makes it so that we have to do *avoda*, and so that we feel it is our responsibility.

sections.title: The reshimu as the source of the Kav: the point and the vav
sections.summary: Like the blueprint, the *reshimu* holds the whole light hidden and is the source of everything in the *Kav*, so the whole chain looks like a set system following one plan. It is the point with two opposites, hiding what is above it and revealing everything to those below; the *Kav* drawn from it is the *vav* whose head is a *yud*, narrower than its source.

phrases.he: וכך בחינת הרשימו הזאת הכוללת ברמז ובקיצור מכל אור העצמות הנעלם בה,
phrases.en: So just like the blueprint, so too this *reshimu* includes in it, in a hinted, in a *kitzur* way, the whole light of the *Atzmus*, which is hidden in it.

phrases.he: הוא עצמו המקור לכל ההמשכות דקו וחוט
phrases.en: This *reshimu* itself is the source for everything that comes out in the *Kav*.
both the *makifim* of the *hishtalshelus* and the *pnimi* of the *hishtalshelus*, from its beginning all the way to its end,

phrases.he: שיהיה הכל כמו שעלה ברצונו וחכמתו הפשוטה בעצמות אור אין סוף ממש כו'
phrases.en: that it should all be according to the way that He originally wanted, with His will and His wisdom, simple will and wisdom, in *Atzmus Or Ein Sof mamash*.

blocks.text: **So just like the blueprint**, this *reshimu* includes in a hinted, *kitzur* way the whole light of the Essence that is hidden in it, and **this reshimu itself is the source for everything that comes out in the Kav.** What does it mean that it is the source? It means that everything that comes out in the rest of the *hishtalshelus* comes through this kind of *tzimtzum*, so the rest of the *hishtalshelus* is all defined by the *reshimu*. Because of this step, everything else is the way it is.

And this is a thing that looks thrown: it looks as if G-d set it up a certain way, set up a certain *hishtalshelus*, and now it goes. That is why, when a lot of people look at Kabbala, it tends to look to them like this machine or something, like a system: because G-d made it like a set thing. And when we understand G-d from that level and down, it is all through this system that He set up.

This holds for both the *makifim* (encompassing lights) and the *pnimi* (inner light) of the *hishtalshelus*, **from its beginning all the way to its end**: everything now comes out according to this *reshimu*, so that **it should all be according to the way that He originally wanted**, with His simple will and wisdom in *Atzmus Or Ein Sof mamash*. So now we see it: the *hishtalshelus* looks as if it is following a plan that G-d decided, a one-time plan. He wants it to come out a certain way, and now it is just following that plan.

blocks.text: This is what is explained elsewhere: a point (*nekuda*), and the *reshimu* is compared to a point, has two aspects, concealment and revelation, **two opposites, two opposite things.** It is **a concealment of everything that's higher than it, relative to it**: the *reshimu* is a *helem* (concealment) of the whole *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*, which is now put into it in a very short and hinted way, so that you don't see it all there. **And it's the source of the revelation of everything to the recipients**: it all comes out from it. The whole *gilui* that the recipients get comes from the *reshimu*.

blocks.title: A funnel, and CliffNotes
blocks.text: It is kind of like a funnel: it takes everything from above, from before it, and channels it all down, and then it all comes out. As we see with the Mishna: the Mishna is like this little, short thing, "like CliffNotes or something," for the way that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi knew the Gemara; but for us it is the source of our whole Gemara.

The revelation that comes to the recipients is the *Kav* that comes from the *reshimu*. The relationship of the *Kav* to the *reshimu* is like the letter *vav*, whose head is a *yud*. The *yud* represents the *reshimu*: it is a point. And then from that point it is drawn down, **as explained elsewhere at length, how the Kav is drawn out from the reshimu.**

If you look at the *vav*, you see that its line is smaller than the *yud*. The *yud*, even though it is like a point, has a little bit of width to it, and the line of the *vav* is very narrow. That is because the *Kav* is less than the *reshimu*. Even though the *reshimu* is like a point, it is a point from the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite): so it is like a zero, but the nothing of the *reshimu* is bigger than everything in our *hishtalshelus*, and the whole *Kav* is really smaller than the *reshimu*.

Whatever comes on the *Kav* never really brings out everything that is hidden in the *reshimu*. It is like the Mishna: even though there is the whole Gemara explaining the Mishna, really there is more in the Mishna, and you can pull out more and more forever. In the same way, it is true that this world follows the *reshimu* and comes out from it, but from the same *roshem* totally different worlds could also come out, as explained elsewhere at length.

sections.title: Summing up: G-d limits Himself so that all is revealed, and the purpose of man is to see past it
sections.summary: The *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu* and the *Kav* are G-d limiting Himself, so to speak, so that this world can be revealed; He hid everything else He could do, and the choosing is itself a revelation. From His own light comes a born light, the *Kav*, like a glowing sheet of metal. The whole of man is to feel this deeply and see past the first *tzimtzum*, and so be bound to G-d Himself.

phrases.he: ובכל זה מובן כללות ענין הצמצום דמקום פנוי
phrases.en: From all of this, we understand the general *inyan* of the *tzimtzum* of the *makom panui*, the empty place *tzimtzum*,
and the impression that was left,
and also the line which comes out from the *reshimu*,

phrases.he: שהוא רק בחינת הגבלה בעצמות כדי שיומשך הכל בגלוי
phrases.en: That the general idea of the *tzimtzum*, *reshimu*, and the *Kav* is that G-d limits Himself, so to speak, in order that everything should be brought out in a revealed way.

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב כי עמך מקור חיים,
phrases.en: This is what it says: With You is the source of life,
and from Your light is seen light,
a born light,
which is the idea of the *Kav*.
like will be explained with the help of G-d,

blocks.text: From all of this the general idea of the *tzimtzum* of the *makom panui* is understood: the empty-place *tzimtzum*, meaning the *tzimtzum* that allowed it to appear that there is something separate from G-d. That is the idea of the empty place: a place that is empty, where you can put something. In order to put things there, you have to empty the space. So this *tzimtzum* made it possible for there to appear to be something separate from G-d, because He hid Himself. **And the impression that was left, and also the line which comes out from the reshimu**: these will be explained more in the next two chapters.

The general idea of the *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu* and the *Kav* is that **G-d limits Himself, so to speak, in order that everything should be brought out in a revealed way.** To reveal the world in the particular way it is now, He hid everything else that He could do. He could have made different worlds and different *sefiros*; He could have done everything in a completely different way. To make it this way, He hid everything else.

But it is not that He lost His potential, and it is not that it is not a complete revelation of Him. In a way it is a greater revelation, because you see that He is choosing how it should be; and choosing that it should be *davka* this way is itself a *gilui* of Him. That is one of the ways the *tzimtzum* itself is a *gilui*.

This is what it says: **With You is the source of life**; from Your light is seen light. What does "from Your light is seen light" mean? From Your light, the light of the *Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, the revelation of G-d Himself, is seen a different light, *or shel tolda*, **a born light**, which is the idea of the *Kav*. A born light means a light that is just induced, an induced light.

blocks.title: The curtain and the glowing metal
blocks.text: For example, if a very strong light shone on a curtain, you would not see the original light; you would just see it coming through the curtain, like a new light. Or, an even better *mashal* in a way: a very strong light shining on an iron curtain, a sheet of metal, where there is no way for the original light to come through. But it heats up the metal, and the metal glows, and a new light comes off. From that light you can see that there must be a light behind it: the fact that it is glowing shows you that there is a light behind it, and you see where the light is concentrated, because it glows brighter there. But you don't see the original thing at all.

That is the way it is. Because of the *tzimtzum*, when we look at the world we see a *gilui* of *chachma* (wisdom) and *middos* (emotional attributes) and all these different things, but we don't see the *gilui* of G-d Himself. Through *avoda* we go past the *tzimtzum* and reveal G-d Himself too. The purpose of the *tzimtzum* is to make it that we have to work to uncover that level: at first we look at the world and don't see the original light. That is why we have to make a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below). **Like will be explained with the help of G-d**, how the *Kav* works.

phrases.en: and this is the whole purpose of man.
to really become very sensitive for this whole idea, that it should really hit you,
and similar things, meaning the rest of the *hishtalshelus* that we're going to explain the rest of the book,

phrases.he: מפני שמזה דוקא יבוא לכלל היחוד האמיתי בהתקשרות נפשו בחיי כל החיים העליונים, שהוא עצמות אור אין סוף ממש מטעם הנזכר לעיל ודי למבין:

blocks.text: This is **the whole purpose of man**: to deepen his *daas* (knowledge) in all this, **to really become very sensitive for this whole idea, that it should really hit you.** We should really feel the idea of the *tzimtzum*, to really appreciate how everything in the *hishtalshelus* is nothing: it is just G-d holding Himself back and revealing just a little bit of what He can do. And we should feel what is behind it, how it is really coming from G-d Himself, and be able to see past the first *tzimtzum*.

That is the main purpose of our *avoda*: to see past the first *tzimtzum*. Even if a person does not *mamash* (actually) see past it, we should live our life with this recognition, have this *daas* for it, really feel it, so that what we connect to, what we feel is important, is G-d Himself. Everything else we should not be so impressed by. We should not consider it important; we should see it only as a means to an end, not as something with intrinsic importance.

When a person has that attitude, he goes with a high hand: he is not impressed by the world or by anything, even by *Gan Eden* (Paradise) and *Olam Haba* (the World to Come), all these things. He just does his *shlichus* (mission), and does what G-d tells him to do. **And similar things**: the rest of the *hishtalshelus*, to be explained in the rest of the book. A person should see through all the *tzimtzumim*. But in a way this is the main one.

Only when a person develops a sensitivity for these things, so that he can see past the different concealments, the hiding that G-d set up in the world, does he come to the true union. That hiding makes it look as if things are set: there is a certain *teva* (nature), and you have to work within that framework; there are limitations, and from that it follows that you can't always do Torah and *mitzvos*, you have to worry about this, you have to worry about that. We want to see past that. Being able to see past these limitations is what allows us to connect to G-d, both because we realize that nothing can stop us, and because we realize what is really important.

We have to fix both our goal and the way we accomplish it. The goal: that our *ratzon* (will) should be only for G-d. And the way: we should realize that we don't have to be affected by all the limitations of the *hishtalshelus*, because the whole reason everything is there is to help us connect to G-d, and so it is impossible for them to stop us. And as was said at the beginning of chapter 12, that is why understanding this lets you direct your *ratzon* to G-d Himself, *v'dai l'mevin*.
